'''''Spergularia marina''''', also called '''''Spergularia salina''''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Caryophyllaceae]] (the pink family).<ref name=TPL_kew-2487483/> It is known as '''salt sandspurry'''<ref>{{Cite book|url=http://www.forest.go.kr/kna/special/download/English_Names_for_Korean_Native_Plants.pdf|title=English Names for Korean Native Plants|publisher=[[Korea National Arboretum]]|year=2015|isbn=978-89-97450-98-5|location=Pocheon|pages=642|access-date=27 December 2016|via=[[Korea Forest Service]]|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170525105020/http://www.forest.go.kr/kna/special/download/English_Names_for_Korean_Native_Plants.pdf|archive-date=25 May 2017}}</ref> or '''lesser sea-spurrey'''.<ref name=BSBI07/> ''S. marina'' is a sprawling [[annual plant|annual]] or sometimes [[perennial plant|perennial]], with stems up to {{cvt|35|cm|0}} long. Like other [[Spergularia|sea-spurrey]] species, its flowers have white to pink [[petal]]s, with [[sepal]]s usually longer than the petals, at {{cvt|2.5|–|4|mm|1}}. Plants are salt-tolerant, being found by the sea and in saline areas inland.<ref name=Stac10/>

==Taxonomy==
The species was first described by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in 1753 as ''Arenaria rubra'' var. ''marina'',<ref name="IPNI_18694-2">{{citation |title=Plant Name Details for ''Arenaria rubra ''var.'' marina'' L. |work=[[International Plant Names Index|The International Plant Names Index]] |url=http://www.ipni.org/ipni/idPlantNameSearch.do?id=18694-2 |access-date=2016-08-03 }}</ref> and was subsequently treated as a full species in different genera, including ''[[Arenaria (plant)|Arenaria]]'' and ''[[Spergula]]''.<ref name=TPL_kew-2487651/> [[The Plant List]] accepts the placement in ''Spergularia'' {{as of|2016|August|lc=yes}}.<ref name=TPL_kew-2487483/> The species was placed in the genus ''Spergularia'' by [[Jan Svatopluk Presl|J.Presl]] and [[Carl Borivoj Presl|C. Presl]] in 1819, who considered the specimens they saw to be a new species (''S. salina''), but several authors had previously elevated Linnaeus' variety to species rank, and the earliest of these brings [[Principle of Priority|nomenclatural priority]], even though that species was transferred to ''Spergularia'' after 1819.<ref>{{harv|McNeill et al.|2012|loc=Article 11|ref=McNeill}}</ref>

The nomenclature has been complicated by some errors.  In 1822 [[Wilibald Swibert Joseph Gottlieb von Besser|Wilibald S. J. G. von Besser]] created the name ''Spergularia marina'', but based his analysis on a 1788 species name in ''Arenaria'' published by [[Albrecht Wilhelm Roth]], who intended to move Linnaeus' variety to a full species. Roth was unaware that [[Carlo Allioni]] had previously, in 1785, elevated the variety to ''Arenaria marina'', so Roth's name is now considered a [[homonym (biology)|homonym]]. Besser's name ''Spergularia marina'' is now considered to be based on Allioni's name and consequently on Linnaeus' variety name; it brings nomenclatural priority from 1785.<ref>{{harv|McNeill et al.|2012|loc=Article 41.8|ref=McNeill}}</ref> A further error that has caused authors to come to different conclusions about the [[correct name (botany)|correct name]] for the species, is a name thought to have been published by [[Peter Simon Pallas]] in 1776. That phantom name came about because [[Carl Friedrich von Ledebour]] cited it after misreading ''Arenaria maritima'' as ''A. marina''.<ref name=Pallas/>
